clue.text: Greek character alone in deep thought?

definitions.note: an adverbial phrase, matching an adverb

parts.note: mu is the twelfth letter of the Greek alphabet
singly means one by one, on its own

explanation.surface: A lone Greek figure sits lost in contemplation.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something in a reflective, pondering way is doing it in deep thought; the question mark flags the loose adverbial match.

clue.text: Mould around vessel upset one of a pair therein?

indicators.note: the mould wraps around the turned vessel

parts.note: must is mould or mustiness

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: Noah's ark is a vessel

explanation.surface: Mould grows round a capsized boat holding a pair of creatures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'therein' points back to the ark, where animals went in two by two, so the definition leans on the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A rodent of North American wetlands would be one of the animal pairs taken aboard Noah's ark.

clue.text: Founder almost gives grave offence

indicators.note: the verb loses its final letter

parts.note: to founder is to sink

explanation.surface: A company's founder very nearly commits a serious crime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Founder' looks like a person; it is the verb meaning to go under.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a serious moral wrong or transgression is a grave offence.

clue.text: This country requires fresh passion also

parts.note: new means fresh
zeal is passionate enthusiasm
and means also, in addition

explanation.surface: A nation demands renewed enthusiasm too.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the Pacific island nation is a country.

clue.text: Legal officer restricting company once

indicators.note: the officer hems in the company, holding it inside

parts.note: Lt is the abbreviation for lieutenant
ICI, Imperial Chemical Industries, was a major British company, since taken over

explanation.surface: A law officer used to restrain a firm.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something lawful and permitted is legal.

clue.text: Ending in pub, one in a hurry for strong drink

indicators.note: the ending of the word pub is its final letter only

parts.note: a racer is someone rushing along at speed

explanation.surface: At closing time in the pub, someone in a rush orders a stiff drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A bracer is an informal name for a stiff tot of spirits taken to fortify oneself.

clue.text: What enables one to lay down the line?

definitions.text: What enables one to lay down the line?

parts.words: What enables one to lay down the line?
parts.note: a ... helps draw straight lines, and governing authority lets one dictate policy

explanation.walkthrough: Two senses blended: the device for drawing a straight line, and authority to dictate how things go.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: a straight-edge for drawing, and governing power to lay down the law.

clue.text: State to hit the right target with one austerity measure?

parts.note: to connect is to land a blow on target
I is the Roman numeral one
a cut in spending is an austerity measure

explanation.surface: A government aims to make spending cuts hit the right people.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the New England territory is one of the US states.

clue.text: After short interval see revolutionary new design

indicators.note: the turned see follows the rest in the answer

parts.note: a rest is a brief pause

indicators.note: turning round, so the see is read backwards

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city and a bishop's see

explanation.surface: After a brief break, a radical new look is unveiled.
explanation.definitionFit: Verb versus noun: to give a new style is to redesign, a fresh design.

clue.text: Murderer with honour is elevated —— one buying his pardon?

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifted up means the letters read from the bottom upward

parts.note: Cain killed his brother Abel
OM, the Order of Merit, is an honour
taken as written

explanation.surface: A killer is honoured, and is portrayed buying forgiveness.
explanation.definitionFit: Simony is paying for church favours or offices, so one guilty of it might purchase absolution.

clue.text: Clans hid as winds swirled in Hawaii a while back

indicators.note: winds that swirled are churning about, so the fodder letters are churned into a new order

explanation.surface: Scottish clans take cover as gales whirl around them.
explanation.walkthrough: Captain Cook named the archipelago after the Earl of Sandwich; the name was used before Hawaii became standard.
explanation.definitionFit: Historical naming: the islands now called Hawaii were known to Europeans by this former name in earlier times.

clue.text: Play about what happened billions of years ago?

parts.note: re is a standard short word for concerning or about

parts.words: what happened billions of years ago?
parts.note: the creation of the universe, the start of everything, took place billions of years back

explanation.surface: A drama about the origins of the cosmos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Play' looks like a noun for a stage drama, which the surface wants; it is the definition in the sense of leisure.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: leisure-time amusement and games are both play and pastime activity.

clue.text: Armed fighter appearing before half-time? Put off game!

parts.note: Che Guevara was a revolutionary guerrilla

indicators.note: only half of the period of time is used, its first three letters

parts.note: a minute is a unit of time
defer means postpone

explanation.surface: A soldier arrives before the interval and the match is postponed.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a card game, a variant of baccarat played in casinos.

clue.text: Wet American who lost two key elections, we hear

indicators.note: signals that the surname is said aloud, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.words: American who lost two key elections
parts.note: Thomas Dewey was the Republican beaten by Roosevelt in 1944 and by Truman in 1948

explanation.surface: A soggy US politician famous for losing two big votes.
explanation.walkthrough: Dewey is the candidate of the famous premature headline 'Dewey Defeats Truman'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something covered with dew, such as morning grass, is damp or moist.

clue.text: Ace divers around Jersey etc keen to grab treasure?

parts.note: A is the card abbreviation for ace

indicators.note: the diverse things surround the islands

parts.note: divers is an old word for various, several
CI is the Channel Islands, of which Jersey is one

explanation.surface: Expert scuba divers around the Channel Islands eager to find sunken treasure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'divers' reads as people swimming underwater; it is the old adjective meaning sundry.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone greedy for wealth is eager to grab riches; the question mark notes the playful phrasing.

clue.text: One held on to shirt? It's seen in bit of film after unsettled game

indicators.note: the bit of film comes after the game in the answer

parts.note: a tie is a drawn game, the result left undecided
a clip is a short extract from a film

explanation.surface: A footballer clings to an opponent's shirt, shown in replay footage after an undecided match.
explanation.definitionFit: A clip fastening a necktie is held against the front of a shirt, keeping the tie in place.

clue.text: Artistic mosaic of yesteryear that is displayed around church

parts.note: past means of former times

indicators.note: the abbreviation for that is spreads around the church

parts.note: i.e. is the Latin abbreviation for that is

explanation.surface: An old artwork of tiles shown around a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A work patched together from bits of other styles is a medley, an artistic mixture or imitation.

clue.text: Get home quickly in Paris to meet English visitor?

parts.note: in means at home
vite is French for quickly

explanation.surface: Hurry home in Paris to greet an English guest.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone asked along to an event is a guest, a kind of visitor; the question mark marks the loose fit.

clue.text: So now the weekend begins, playmates!

definitions.meaning: once Friday is over, Saturday and Sunday start

explanation.surface: Children cheer the start of the weekend and their chums.
explanation.definitionFit: Playmates are companions and pals, people one spends free time with, close mates.

clue.text: Central government's got wild about leader writer maybe

indicators.note: the wild word goes around the writer

parts.note: feral means wild
an editor, ED, may write the paper's leaders, its editorials

explanation.surface: The national administration has gone wild over a newspaper columnist.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjective sense: belonging to a national authority over the states, as in a union's government.

clue.text: A vehicle almost bumping into others in the capital

indicators.note: one piece runs into the middle of the other, as a car collides with others

parts.note: the other vehicles, cars

indicators.note: the vehicle loses its last letter

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A car nearly crashes into other traffic in a city centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'others' means other vehicles here, matching the vehicle that bumps into them.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the city is the capital of Venezuela.

clue.text: Misery these days seen in various directions

indicators.note: the era is seen inside the points of the compass

parts.note: S, N, E, S are compass points
AD, anno Domini, is the present era

explanation.surface: Unhappiness is found everywhere nowadays.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: unhappiness or sorrow is misery.

clue.text: Appeal to parent to replace part of wall specially decorated

indicators.note: the appeal is put in a new place, moved from the front to the back

parts.note: O is an exclamation of appeal, as in 'O God'
dad is a parent

explanation.surface: A plea to a father to redecorate a bit of the wall.
explanation.walkthrough: The appeal 'O, Dad' has its O moved by 'to replace' from the front to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: the lower section of an interior wall, often panelled or papered differently from above, is this feature.

clue.text: Very little shown to be justified

parts.note: V is the short form of very, a little version of the word
indicated means pointed out or shown

explanation.surface: Hardly anything was demonstrated to have been fair.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone proved right or cleared of blame has been justified.

clue.text: Endure rejection so much as artist

indicators.note: the answer is only so much as a portion of the two words, sitting within them

explanation.surface: An artist must put up with rejection.
explanation.definitionFit: Albrecht Dürer was a German Renaissance painter and engraver.

clue.text: One bird won't have nibbled another one

indicators.note: means that the bird lacks the nibbled part

parts.note: another bird, the bittern, a heron
bit is the past tense of bite, nibbled

explanation.surface: One bird refuses to peck at another.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a sea bird related to gulls is a bird.

clue.text: Lectures for old hands? It's right to demand payment to let in new student

indicators.note: the outer piece admits the other within it

parts.note: recourse is a legal right to demand payment or compensation
a fresher is a first-year student at university

explanation.surface: Talks for veterans, where it's correct to charge admission to a beginner.
explanation.definitionFit: Training that updates experienced staff on their skills is lectures given to old hands; the question mark marks the playful description.

clue.text: What stroke does, we hear, for shy animal

indicators.note: signals that the word is spoken and spelt another way

parts.note: the stroke in a rowing crew rows, setting the rhythm

explanation.surface: What a swimming stroke does for a timid creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stroke' suggests swimming or petting; it is the oarsman nearest the stern.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a small, timid European deer is a shy animal.

clue.text: Stories by 3 person who investigated behaviour

parts.note: lore is a body of traditional tales
refers to the answer at 3 down, the country, abbreviated NZ

explanation.surface: A storyteller from a far country who studied conduct.
explanation.definitionFit: Konrad Lorenz, the Austrian ethologist, won a Nobel prize for studying animal behaviour.

clue.text: From which many regulations sprout?

parts.note: the Belgian capital is the seat of the EU, which issues many rules, and also gives its name to a green vegetable, the sprout

explanation.walkthrough: 'sprout' plays on the green vegetable named after the city; the European Commission there issues rules.
explanation.definitionFit: Metonymy: the city name stands for EU bureaucracy, the source of so many rules.
